$comment: wp-ja-kinetic — what the theme reads from each article, author, tag and page that WordPress core does not store, and where each value comes from on the Joomla source. Sibling to patterns.map.json (the seeder's ACM-section contract). The toolkit's `scripts/seed.mjs` does not read this file: every duty below that says "written by post-seed" is carried, for this run, by `tasks/ja-kinetic-wp7/post-seed.mjs` (D-34, 2026-09-24), which reads the source database (SELECT only) and writes through WP-CLI after EVERY seed run (order: seed.mjs, then post-seed; both re-run to nothing changed). Teaching the toolkit these duties is parked, not rejected (D-34 road A).
carriedBy: tasks/ja-kinetic-wp7/post-seed.mjs + post-seed.php (D-34). Besides the keys below it also writes: `users_can_register` from the source's com_users `allowUserRegistration`; `wp_ja_kinetic_list` / `wp_ja_kinetic_page_template` on the list pages (inc/list-pages.php, D-33); and testimonial role+company / avatar alt in the seeded page content. It creates only the users the source's articles are credited to (not test users registered on the source).

tags.description: The single-tag view's masthead subtitle (`com_tags/tag/default.php:47-49`, `.kinetic-tags-sub`) is the tag's own `description` field — WordPress's `wp:term-description` block already reads this natively (`get_term_field('description', ...)`, no new key needed), but the WordPress `post_tag` taxonomy term this theme's tags map onto carries NO description unless the seeder writes one: `wp_set_post_tags()` only ever creates a bare term by name. Proven live 2026-09-22: with no description set the subtitle renders an empty (but present) `<div>`; setting `wp_update_term($tag_id, 'post_tag', ['description' => $value])` from the source's tag description reproduced the source's subtitle text exactly. Written by post-seed: each tag's source description onto the matching `post_tag` term (`tr_tags.description`).
tags.assignmentOrder: The source's related-posts eyebrow (`article/default_related.php:56-71`) picks a related post's FIRST tag by `tag_date ASC` — the order tags were assigned to that article in Joomla, not alphabetical. `blocks/related-posts/render.php` reads the WordPress equivalent: `wp_get_object_terms( $id, 'post_tag', array( 'orderby' => 'term_order' ) )`, taking index 0. `term_order` is WordPress's own assignment-order column in `wp_term_relationships` — but core never populates it for `post_tag` by default (that taxonomy has no `sort` support; verified in `wp-includes/taxonomy.php:2963`, `if ( ! $append && isset( $t->sort ) && $t->sort )` — the column stays 0 for every relationship without it). `inc/extra.php`'s `wp_ja_kinetic_sort_post_tags()` opts `post_tag` into `sort` on `init`, which is what makes `term_order` carry real assignment order at all. Given that: post-seed sets each article's tags with `wp_set_object_terms()` in the SAME ORDER the source assigned them (`tr_contentitem_tag_map.tag_date` ascending) — not alphabetised, not reordered.
tags.verified: 2026-09-22, on a live page render (not just a DB check): a probe post's sibling carried tags assigned in the literal order `zeta`, `alpha`, `metrics` (deliberately non-alphabetical). `wp post_tag` on it (with the sort fix active) recorded `term_order` 1/2/3 in that same order. The related-posts card for that sibling rendered eyebrow `ZETA` — the first-ASSIGNED tag, not `ALPHA` (first alphabetically) and not `METRICS` (last assigned).
tags.sourceTagIdMeta: The article tag list prints each tag's SOURCE (Joomla) tag id as the `tag-{id}` class on its `<li>` (`layouts/joomla/content/tags.php`; e.g. `li.list-inline-item.tag-7.tag-list0` for `incident`). WordPress cannot choose a term id, so `inc/tag-parity.php` reads term meta `wp_ja_kinetic_source_tag_id` and falls back to the term id when it is missing. Written by post-seed: each `post_tag` term's source tag id there. Proven live 2026-09-23 on singles 138/76: with the meta set to the source ids (incident 7, alerting 14, opentelemetry 6, dashboards 9) the tag list measured nodes 5/5/m5, onlySrc=0, onlyWp=0 at 1440 and 390; without it, the two `li` differ only by that id.

authors.displayAlias: The single/article byline name itself can be a per-article Joomla `created_by_alias`, overriding the real author's name for that one post (`article/default.php`; measured live, single article id 76's byline reads "Tracy Agent" though the real Joomla user differs). `inc/item-ids.php`'s `wp_ja_kinetic_author_alias_override()` reads it from post meta `wp_ja_kinetic_article_author_alias`; unset, the WordPress user's own display name shows, unchanged. Written by post-seed per article (post or page) from the source's `created_by_alias` (empty where the source has none).
authors.articleRole: The single-article byline role (`.hx-author__meta`, e.g. "Head of Product · 04 July 2026 · 2 min read") is a PER-ARTICLE Joomla custom field (`author_role`, `article/default.php:72-78`), independent of the author's general job title — proven live 2026-09-22: two articles credited to the same person rendered different role text for the byline (one carried a role, one carried none), which the per-user `wp_ja_kinetic_job_title` field cannot express. `blocks/article-byline-meta/render.php` reads a post meta key this theme defines for it, `wp_ja_kinetic_article_author_role`; unset it renders no role segment at all (not a fallback to the user's job title). Written by post-seed per article from the source's `author_role` field (`tr_fields_values`), separately from the per-user job title.
authors.jobTitle: The source's author card/aside carries a job title (`.hx-aucard__r` on the authors index, `.hx-auaside__role` on the single-author view — e.g. "Staff SRE", "Co-founder & CTO") from a Joomla custom profile plugin field. WordPress core has no matching user field, so this theme reads it from a user meta key it defines for that purpose: `wp_ja_kinetic_job_title` (plain string, `get_the_author_meta( 'wp_ja_kinetic_job_title', $user_id )`). Written by post-seed from the source's `profile.user_jobtitle` (`tr_user_profiles`) for every author; a user with no value simply renders without the role line/pill (`blocks/author-identity/render.php`, `blocks/authors-directory/render.php`) — not an error, but every author the source shows a title for should carry one after seeding, or the pages are not D-11-identical.
authors.bio: The source's author bio (single-author view only) already maps to a WordPress core field with no new key needed: `get_the_author_meta( 'description', $user_id )` — post-seed writes it there from the source's `profile.aboutme`.
authors.tagline: The single-author masthead subtitle (`author.php:50-53`) reads a THIRD, distinct field ahead of bio/job-title: `profile.get('user_tagline')`, falling back to the bio, then to the job title, only when each prior one is empty. WordPress has no core field for it; this theme reads it from `wp_ja_kinetic_user_tagline` user meta (`get_the_author_meta( 'wp_ja_kinetic_user_tagline', $user_id )`, filtered onto the core `post-author-biography` block's own `get_the_author_description` output in `inc/blog-dynamic.php`'s `wp_ja_kinetic_author_masthead_sub()`). Written by post-seed from the source's `profile.user_tagline` for every author that has one; an author with none simply falls through to bio then job title, same as the source.
authors.directorySelection: `/product/authors` selects by Joomla USER-GROUP membership (`author.php`'s `$authorsUrl` builds `…&gid[0]=3`, the "Author" group) — NOT by who has a published post. Measured live 2026-09-22: the source lists exactly Priya Raman, Arjun Mehta, Lena Park, Tomás Rivera, in that order, which matches those four Joomla users' `id` ascending (551-554, i.e. Joomla-user-creation order) exactly; a fifth user with a published post but in a different group ("Tracy Agent") does NOT appear. `blocks/authors-directory/render.php` selects WordPress's own "Author" role (`role: 'author'`) ordered by `ID` ASC as the closest equivalent relationship. Post-seed creates the users the source's articles are credited to, in the source's `id` order, with the WordPress "Author" role for the source's group-3 members and "Editor" for the others (Tracy Agent, group 8) — so the directory's membership and order match D-11.
authors.photo: Every author card (`/product/authors`, the single-author aside) reads a real uploaded portrait, `images/people/<slug>.jpg` (`author_helper.php::kinetic_au_photo()`), falling back to computed initials only when that file is missing — measured live, all 4 seeded authors have one on the source. WordPress core has no per-user photo field; this theme reads a full attachment URL from a user meta key it defines for that purpose, `wp_ja_kinetic_user_photo` (`get_the_author_meta( 'wp_ja_kinetic_user_photo', $user_id )`, filtered onto `get_avatar()` via `pre_get_avatar_data` in `inc/blog-dynamic.php`'s `wp_ja_kinetic_avatar_real_photo()`). Written by post-seed: each author's source portrait (`images/people/<login with dots as dashes>.jpg`) — the attachment the seeder already imported for that file where there is one, else imported — and its URL onto this key; a user with no value falls through to WordPress's own gravatar/default-image behaviour, same as today — not D-11-identical for an author the source has a real photo for. Confirmed by probe run 3 (2026-09-23, `_r3probe_listings2`): imported the source's own `images/people/priya-raman.jpg` as a media attachment and set it on user 30 (`r3p-priya.raman`) via `wp user meta update 30 wp_ja_kinetic_user_photo <attachment guid>` — `/product/authors/` and `/author/r3p-priya-raman/` then rendered the real portrait at the source's own box size/position (72px card avatar, 88px aside avatar) with `aria-hidden="true"` already applied (no theme change needed, `wp_ja_kinetic_avatar_aria_hidden()` already covers it); the other 3 unseeded authors kept the gravatar silhouette on the same render, isolating this as SEED only, no THEME gap. Attachment and user meta deleted after measuring (audit rows L-66, L-68).

listingExcerpts.source: Every blog/category/author listing row excerpt on the source reads the article's `introtext` (source `category/blog_item.php:47`, `category/thumbs_item.php:44`, `category/blog.php:184` [the featured card], `author/author_posts.php:31` — all `trim(strip_tags($item->introtext))`), NOT `metadesc`. Measured live 2026-09-22, `/product/blog` row for article 193: source excerpt is the article's own lead sentence; the WordPress stand rendered its `metadesc` field instead (audit row L-30/L-49) because `post_excerpt` was seeded from `metadesc`. Written by post-seed: every article's `post_excerpt` (post, and page — a page such as `/pages/helixql` is a row of its category's blog list too) is the source's `introtext`, stripped of tags, untruncated (the theme truncates at render time, see `truncation` below). The article's own sub-title prints `metadesc` instead — see `contentPages.excerpt`.
listingExcerpts.truncation: FIXED 2026-09-23 (THEME, not SEED): the source truncates each listing excerpt with `HTMLHelper::_('string.truncate', $text, $length, true, false)` — a character-based cut at the last whole word within `$length`, appending a literal three-dot `...` — a different algorithm from WordPress core's own word-count `wp_trim_words()` (which `core/post-excerpt`'s `excerptLength` attribute uses, single-character `…`). `inc/blog-dynamic.php`'s `wp_ja_kinetic_joomla_truncate()` ports the source method's `allowHtml=false` branch and is applied via a `render_block` filter on `core/post-excerpt` (`wp_ja_kinetic_truncate_post_excerpt()`, keyed by the block's `className`) and directly in `blocks/field-notes-featured/render.php` for the featured card. Lengths per source call site: blog + the 5 child-category rows 130 (`className hx-blogexcerpt`), engineering cards 120 (`hxcat-row__excerpt`), author archive rows 110 (`hx-aupost__e`), featured card 180. None of the listing templates set `core/post-excerpt`'s `excerptLength` attribute any more — `get_the_excerpt()` must reach the filter with the full, untruncated `post_excerpt` (see `source` above), or the render-time cut has the wrong input. Verified live 2026-09-23 against the source's own truncation of article 165's introtext (153 chars, length 130): both the source and this function cut to the identical string "Nobody warned me the hardest part wouldn't be the technical debugging. It would be trusting myself enough to act on what the...".

contentPages.which: Every `step2/spec/page-map.json` entry with `view: "page"` AND `source.view: "article"` — measured 2026-09-22: exactly product-features, product-integrations, product-changelog, product-faq, pricing, company-about, company-team, pages-helixql, privacy-policy, terms-of-service (their `.file` values). The source has no distinct "page" content type — each of these is a plain `com_content` article (`source.view: "article"`, `source.id` the Joomla article id) reached through its own menu item, the same as a blog post; every OTHER `view: "page"` entry (`page-landing`, `page-authors`, `page-categories`, `page-tags`, …) has a different `source.view` (`featured`, `author`, `categories`, `tags`, …) and must NOT get this treatment.
contentPages.template: Post-seed sets `wp_ja_kinetic_page_template = 'page-article'` on each of the ten pages above — not `_wp_page_template`, which `seed.mjs` rewrites to its own choice on every run; `inc/list-pages.php` puts this key's template first in the page hierarchy — so they render through `templates/page-article.html` — the same D-11 frame as `templates/single.html` — instead of the generic `templates/page.html`. Verified live 2026-09-22: without this meta a Page falls through to `page.html`, which has none of the source's article chrome (masthead band, byline, related posts, CTA 235) — that gap is the whole of audit rows C-37..C-40 / SA-01..SA-08 / SB-01..SB-05.
contentPages.category: The breadcrumb + eyebrow pill on these pages (`wp:post-terms {"term":"category"}` in `templates/page-article.html`) read the WordPress `category` taxonomy, which this overlay now attaches to the `page` post type (`inc/item-ids.php`, `wp_ja_kinetic_register_page_taxonomies()`) — a Page carries no category term until post-seed writes one. The source category name is NOT always "Uncategorised": measured live, `/pages/helixql` breadcrumbs "Field notes from the on-call" (the same category the blog posts use) and `/privacy-policy`/`/terms-of-service` breadcrumb "Legal" — post-seed reads each article's real Joomla category (`catid` → the spec's `categories[].wpSlug`).
contentPages.tags: Only some of the ten carry `post_tag` terms on the source (measured live: `/pages/helixql` does — `opentelemetry`, `logs`, rendered by the same `wp:post-terms {"term":"post_tag"}` block `templates/single.html` uses); most do not, and the block renders nothing when a Page has none, matching the source. Same assignment-order rule as the `tags` key above (first-assigned tag drives the related-posts eyebrow) applies here too, on the `page` post type as well as `post`.
contentPages.byline: Byline (initials + name + role/date/read-time) reads the same fields the `authors` key above documents (`wp_ja_kinetic_article_author_role` post meta, `post_author`), on the `page` post type as well as `post` — `blocks/author-initials`, `blocks/article-byline-meta` are post-type-agnostic already.
contentPages.infoBlock: The hidden article foot (`blocks/article-foot`) prints `footer.hx-article__foot` only when the source article's `attribs.info_block_position` is 1 or 2 (`article/default.php`). Measured on the source DB 2026-09-23: every blog article carries 1; the Uncategorised shell articles (features/integrations/changelog/faq/pricing, ids 90-94) and Legal (privacy/terms, ids 88/89) carry `{}` (global default 0, no footer); `/pages/helixql` carries 1. Written by post-seed as post meta `wp_ja_kinetic_info_block_position` on every article (post or page), the global default where the article's `attribs` carries none; unset, the block falls back to 1 for a post and 0 for a page.
contentPages.excerpt: The sub-title under the h1 (`wp:post-excerpt {className: hx-article__sub}` in single.html / page-article.html) prints the source's `metadesc` (`html/com_content/article/default.php:147-148`), and only when it is set: measured live, `/pages/helixql`, `/privacy-policy` and `/terms-of-service` render a `.hx-article__sub`; `/pricing`, `/company/about`, `/company/team` do not. `post_excerpt` cannot hold it — every list row prints the article's `introtext` from there (`listingExcerpts.source`) and the two differ on most articles — so post-seed writes `metadesc` to post meta `wp_ja_kinetic_metadesc` on every article, and `inc/item-ids.php` prints that key in the sub-title (nothing when it is empty; a post or page without the key keeps its stored excerpt as before).
contentPages.intro:
On `/privacy-policy` and `/terms-of-service` the source prints the intro sentence ("How Helix collects…" / "The terms governing…") as bare text directly inside `.article-body`, not in a `

`. It must be written as bare text in front of the first block (not a `core/paragraph`, and not as plain HTML with no blocks — `wpautop` then wraps it in `

` again). Probe 2026-09-23 (pages 1356/1357, deleted): bare-text intro gives box 0, px 0% against the source; the wrapped form adds ~21px. Not written by post-seed: `/privacy-policy` and `/terms-of-service` measure 15/15 runs in step 8; the box/pixel check belongs to step 8b.
contentPages.related: `blocks/related-posts/render.php` queries `post_type => array('post','page')` (not just `post`) so a Page's related band can surface sibling Pages in the same category, matching the source's flat article model (no content-type filter) — verified live: `/product/features` relates to Integrations/Changelog/FAQ (other Pages, same "Uncategorised" category), `/pages/helixql` relates to blog POSTS, `/privacy-policy` relates to only `/terms-of-service`. Dates, measured on the source 2026-09-24: every list row and related card prints and orders by `created` (`default_related.php:47,85`, `blog_item.php`); an article's byline prints `created` when the merged `show_create_date` is on and `publish_up` otherwise (`article/default.php:188-192`; global `show_create_date` 0, the Blog 221 and Engineering 253 menu items set it to 1). So post-seed writes `post_date` = `created` on every article, and on an article whose own menu item leaves the global default it also writes `wp_ja_kinetic_byline_date` = `publish_up`, which `blocks/article-byline-meta` prints. `/pages/helixql`: `created` 2026-06-22 09:00 (its blog row "Jun 22 2026"), `publish_up` 2026-06-20 09:00 (its byline "20 June 2026"). An earlier revision of this key called 2026-06-20 its `created`; that value is its `publish_up`.

relatedPostsReadTimeAndOrder.readTime: FIXED 2026-09-22 (THEME, not SEED — no seeder action needed): `blocks/related-posts/render.php` was calling `wp_ja_kinetic_readtime( get_the_content() )` inside its own secondary `WP_Query` loop; `get_the_content()` there returns only the TEASER text (before a post's `<!--more-->` split) because `WP_Query::generate_postdata()` only unlocks the full body when `get_queried_object_id() === $post->ID && ($this->is_page() || $this->is_single())`, which is never true for a manually-built secondary query. Fixed by reading `get_post_field( 'post_content', get_the_ID() )` (the raw field, no teaser split) instead. Verified live: a 326-word related post read "1 min" before the fix and "2 min" (matching the source exactly) after, using the SAME `wp_ja_kinetic_readtime()` formula (`inc/blog-dynamic.php`, unchanged) — the formula was always correct, only the teaser-truncated input was wrong.
relatedPostsReadTimeAndOrder.tieBreakOrder: FIXED 2026-09-22 (THEME): two source related items can share the exact same `created` timestamp to the second; the source still renders a fixed, repeatable order (lower Joomla article id first, measured live). `blocks/related-posts/render.php`'s query orders `date DESC`, then the source article id (post meta `wp_ja_kinetic_source_article_id`, written by post-seed), then `ID` — WordPress ids follow seeding order, which is not the source's for pages (2026-09-24: `/product/features` listed Pricing, Joomla 94, first by WordPress id).

categoryIcon.termMetaKey: The source's category card icon (`.hx-cat-ic`, an inline Lucide SVG, `/product/all-categories`) has no stored value on the source: `tr_fields` holds only `company` and `author_role`, and no category's `params` carries an icon (read 2026-09-24) — the source's own template picks it. `blocks/categories-index/render.php` reads it from a term meta key this theme defines: `wp_ja_kinetic_icon` on the `category` taxonomy term (`get_term_meta( $term_id, 'wp_ja_kinetic_icon', true )`), a Lucide icon name (e.g. `grid-2x2`, `heart-pulse`) — NOT raw SVG markup, since the block validates it against its own fixed inline-SVG set before ever echoing anything. A category the seeder does not set this on falls back, in order, to the block's own hardcoded map for the six categories the source was measured with (engineering/incident-retros/product/tutorials/practice/culture), then the source's own unknown-icon glyph (`kinetic_fl_lucide()`'s fallback, `acm/features-ledger/tmpl/style-1.php`). Nothing to write: the block's own map for those six categories is the source's choice; the key stays available for a site owner.

provision.acymailing: D-12: the footer newsletter band (`parts/footer.html`, `.tracy-footer__news-row`) renders the block `acymailing/subscription-form`, which is unregistered (renders nothing) until the plugin is installed. Not a seeder or post-seed duty: the WordPress provisioner (tch fleet, per-design plugin list, D-13) installs and activates AcyMailing for WordPress from wordpress.org, slug `acymailing`, the same 11.0.5 this overlay's PHP was read against (`inc/extra.php`'s `wp_ja_kinetic_dequeue_acymailing_module_css()` and `wp_ja_kinetic_newsletter_placeholder()` both cite that version's file:line; a materially different version should be re-verified against those two functions before shipping). No form record needs creating: the block is attribute-driven, not tied to a saved `wp_acym_form` row — verified live, `wp_acym_form` stayed empty (0 rows) throughout. Activation itself is sufficient: AcyMailing seeds one default list (measured id 1, name "Newsletters") automatically, and the block's own defaults (no `hiddenlists`/`displists` set) subscribe silently to every list that exists — which is why the source's own hidden `hiddenlists value="1"` field and this WordPress block reach the same end state without the seeder having to name a list explicitly. Everything else the source's form needs (email-only field, "Subscribe" button text, no consent line, the placeholder swap to "you@company.com", the plugin's own admin-UI stylesheet dequeued so it cannot fight the chrome sheet) is already baked into the committed `parts/footer.html` block attributes and `inc/extra.php` — nothing else to configure at provision time. Verified 2026-09-22: install+activate on the stand (`wp plugin install acymailing --activate`, downloaded from `downloads.wordpress.org/plugin/acymailing.11.0.5.zip` on the host, since the stand's own container has no outbound network) reproduced the source's footer newsletter band at identical height at 1440 and 390.

authPages.titles: The four auth pages' own masthead h1 reads WordPress `post-title` (`templates/page-login.html`, `page-register.html`, `page-password.html`), i.e. the Page's own post title — the source prints its menu item's `page_heading` param there. Post-seed writes each account page's `post_title` from the source menu's `page_heading` (`tr_menu.params`): `/pages/login` "Sign in to Helix", `/pages/register` "Create your Helix account", `/pages/reset` "Reset your password", `/pages/remind` "Forgot your username?" (step 8 2026-09-24: all four routes match).

articleDates.postDateFromCreated: The source's blog/category listings order and print the article's `created` date (menu `order_date: "created"`; `blog_item.php:52` uses `$item->created`), not `publish_up`. The stand's `post_date` currently holds the source's `publish_up` (article 87: publish_up 2026-06-14, created 2026-06-25 → WP post 763 post_date 2026-06-14), so the category page 2 order differs (proven 2026-09-23: the source's catid 22 list ordered by `publish_up DESC, id ASC` reproduces WordPress's order exactly). Written by post-seed: `post_date` = the source's `created` on every article (see `contentPages.related` for the byline date).

articleFoot.hitsMeta: The single article's hidden footer (`footer.hx-article__foot > dl.article-info`, `display:none` on the source) prints the Joomla hit counter (`dd.hits`). `blocks/article-foot/render.php` always prints it with the value of post meta `wp_ja_kinetic_hits` (0 when unset). Written by post-seed from each article's `hits` as the step-2 dump recorded it (`step2/j6/inventory.json`, 2026-09-21) — not the live table: the source counts every page view, so step 8's own visits would move the value between runs (coordinator, 2026-09-24) so the value matches (no visual effect: the subtree is hidden).
